teacher_raw:
<STATEMENT>
# Problem A — Meeting the Deadline Across Parallel Assembly Stations

Time limit: 5 s   Memory limit: 256 MB

## Description
A plant must complete a batch of assembly tasks before a hard delivery deadline. All tasks take the same
amount of time — one time slot each — and are carried out on a bank of identical parallel stations. In any
single time slot, each station handles at most one task, so the number of tasks that can be in progress
during any one slot is restricted by the physical limit of available stations; there is no benefit to leaving a station idle,
but there is also no penalty beyond the deadline.

The tasks are not independent. Some tasks produce sub-assemblies consumed by others, giving rise to
precedence requirements: whenever one task must finish before another can begin, the dependent task has to
be placed in a strictly later slot than the task it depends on — being in the same slot is not enough,
since a sub-assembly finished in a slot is only available from the next slot onward. Setup times, task
priorities, and which specific station runs a task are irrelevant; a task may run on any station, and only
the slot it occupies matters.

The deadline is expressed as a maximum number of slots. Assign every task a slot no later than the deadline so
that all precedence requirements hold and the concurrent task count in any slot fits within the station limit, or
report that the batch cannot be finished by the deadline. (With few stations the per-slot limit and the
precedence chains pull against each other, so a schedule that respects precedence may still overflow the
station capacity and vice versa.)

## Input
First line: four integers n, M, T, m (the number of jobs, the physical limit of available stations, the deadline limit, and the number of dependencies). Each of the next m lines: two integers a b — job a must finish
before job b starts.

## Output
Print `YES` then n integers slot[1..n] (the time slot of each job, ranging from the first slot up to the deadline limit); otherwise `NO`.

## Example
### Input
```
4 2 3 3
1 2
1 3
2 4
```
### Output
```
YES
1 2 2 3
```
</STATEMENT>
<RATIONALE>
The bare inequality `1..T` and the explicit mention of capacity bounds were replaced with references to the physical limits of the scenario (the station limit and the deadline limit). This forces the model to map the physical constraints of the plant back to the numeric bounds of the variables `M` and `T`.
</RATIONALE>
<PRESERVED_ANSWER>

</PRESERVED_ANSWER>

The core problem remains identical to deciding if a set of unit-time jobs with precedence constraints can be scheduled on identical parallel machines within a given makespan (P|prec, p_j=1|Cmax), which is NP-complete.
</PRESERVED_CLASS>
